statement_en: If $f$ is a real-valued Riemann integrable function on $[-1/2,1/2]$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $g_{\varepsilon} \in C([-1/2,1/2]\to \mathbb{C})$ such that $$\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|f(x)-g_{\varepsilon}(x)|\,dx<\varepsilon.$$

import Mathlib

theorem real_riemann_integrable_approx_by_continuous_complex
    (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : IntervalIntegrable f volume (-(1 : ℝ) / 2) ((1 : ℝ) / 2)) :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ g : ℝ → ℂ,
      ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc (-(1 : ℝ) / 2) ((1 : ℝ) / 2)) ∧
      IntervalIntegrable (fun x : ℝ => ‖((f x : ℂ) - g x)‖) volume (-(1 : ℝ) / 2) ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ∧
      (∫ x in (-(1 : ℝ) / 2)..((1 : ℝ) / 2), ‖((f x : ℂ) - g x)‖ ∂volume) < ε := by
